issues.legal_issue: Restitution under Section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be ordered when a decree is varied or modified, including by restoring property sold in execution of the original decree.
A decree-holder who purchases property in execution of the decree, and a person claiming through that decree-holder, are not protected from restitution as bona fide third-party purchasers.
A third-party purchaser with knowledge of pending litigation concerning the decree is not entitled to resist restitution as a bona fide purchaser.

An executing court is obligated to sell only the portion of attached property necessary to satisfy the decree, and a sale of the entire property without assessing whether a smaller portion would suffice is illegal.
Setting aside the execution sale was the appropriate restitution where the decree was reduced and the sale of all attached properties at a low price caused substantial loss to the judgment debtor.
